quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will enter the road ahead.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagon signs are always stop signs. When you see one, you must stop completely. Let any other traffic or pedestrians pass first, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: As a rider, how can you reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Do not look ahead for hazards.
Do not use turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.
Make sure other drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make yourself visible to other drivers, use clear signals, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, watch the road ahead, and spot hazards early. Always be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other drinks?

options.text: It does not affect the body.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It passes through the stomach and small intestine walls directly into the blood, reaching the brain quickly.

questions.question: What is the most important way to get protection from your helmet?
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets safety standards, fits snugly all around your head, and has no damage.

questions.question: What do you do as your motorcycle speeds up?
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle accelerates, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: How should a protective jacket fit?

options.text: Loose so it flaps in the wind.

questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you and keep you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snug enough that they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If you speed up, they may just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: It is not safe to use.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: It builds up in your body faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your blood. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink per hour, alcohol will stay in your system.

questions.question: What removes alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. There is no way to speed up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light means the red light is coming next. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have footrests for both you and your passenger. This keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it difficult for drivers to see a motorcycle's turn signals, the rider should:

options.text: Continue to use the mechanical turn signals.
Honk their horn to inform other drivers of any upcoming turns.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not make sudden movements, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make sudden movements, if possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: There may be less traction available for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is straight up and down.
A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans during a turn, there is less grip available for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stare straight in front of their motorcycle.
Be unwilling to move to avoid a potential hazard.
Scan ahead of their motorcycle, looking 10 to 15 seconds down the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan ahead of their motorcycle, looking 10 to 15 seconds down the road.
questions.explanation: Look ahead 10 to 15 seconds on the road to reduce crashes. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what's happening both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: It is most important to watch the road ahead. But you also need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, mirrors:

options.text: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
Should be used only by the lead rider.
Should not be checked frequently because they can be a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked frequently by all riders.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, check your mirrors often. This helps you watch the other riders and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of a head or neck injury?
questions.explanation: A quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries when riding a motorcycle. Speed does not prevent these injuries.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. Who must yield?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal that the other vehicle should proceed.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What should an ideal lane position do?

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Invite others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you out of blind spots, away from wind blasts and road hazards, and discourages other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Leather boots protect your feet and ankles the best. They should be high and sturdy enough to support your ankles.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because a motorcycle is usually smaller than a car

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
